cues.title: Float the first entrance
cues.text: Begin with a clean, speech-sized onset. Keep the breath moving through the line instead of adding weight to announce the first note.

cues.title: Keep the wide phrase in one shape
cues.text: This phrase spans almost an octave. Let vowels stay narrow and connected so each pitch change comes from the melody, not a new jaw position.

cues.title: Let vibrato arrive after the pitch
cues.text: Land the center first, then release the sustained tone. The recording adds vibrato generously here; avoid manufacturing it with jaw movement.

cues.title: Sustain without pressing
cues.text: The contour becomes very stable here. Use steady ribs and a small vowel so the held line stays even while intensity grows.

cues.title: Turn the run as one gesture
cues.text: This compact phrase moves through a wide range quickly. Practice it on one neutral vowel, then restore the words without punching each note.

cues.title: Prepare the octave-sized turn
cues.text: Largest measured pitch span in the song occurs here. Hear the destination before starting and keep the lower note light so the upper pitch does not need a push.

cues.title: Separate agility from vibrato
cues.text: Fast pitch changes and vibrato overlap here. First sing the note sequence straight and rhythmically; add the released tail only after the run is accurate.

cues.title: Aim high notes forward
cues.text: This entrance reaches one of the song’s highest areas. Keep consonants quick, maintain a tall inner vowel, and resist lifting the chin.

cues.title: Spend intensity, not extra air
cues.text: These are among the strongest and most sustained moments. Increase resonance and intention while keeping airflow economical so the phrase remains controlled.

cues.title: Shape the long release
cues.text: The final extended phrase stays high and uses recurring vibrato. Plan one dynamic arc: arrive, bloom, then taper without letting pitch collapse as volume fades.
